name: Senseair S8 LP CO2 sensor
description: Senseair S8 LP NDIR carbon dioxide sensor, 400–10000 ppm (±40 ppm ±3 % from 400–2500 ppm), new reading every 4 s, read over a 3.3 V UART with Modbus RTU at 9600 baud. Needs a 4.5–5.25 V supply. Sold as: Senseair S8 LP module, article 004-0-0053 (bare module, 4-pin edge G+, G0, Alarm_OC, PWM 1kHz and 5-pin edge DVCC_out, UART_RxD, UART_TxD, UART_R/T, bCAL_in).
eli5: Measures how much carbon dioxide is in the room, so you know when it is time to open a window.

pins.name: G+
pins.description: Supply plus, 4.5–5.25 V (5 V). Not protected against reverse polarity!

pins.name: Alarm_OC
pins.description: Open-collector alarm output, pulled up to G+ (5 V) inside: do not wire straight to a 3.3 V GPIO

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: PWM 1kHz output, 3.3 V push-pull, 0–100 % duty = 0–2000 ppm

pins.name: DVCC_out
pins.description: 3.3 V regulator output, max 6 mA (for a level shifter only; leave unconnected otherwise)

pins.name: UART_RxD
pins.description: UART receive (3.3 V logic): connect to the board's TX

pins.name: UART_TxD
pins.description: UART transmit (3.3 V logic): connect to the board's RX

pins.name: UART_R/T
pins.description: Direction output for an RS485 transceiver; not needed for direct UART

pins.name: bCAL_in
pins.description: Calibration input: pull to G0 for 4–8 s = background calibration at 400 ppm, 16 s+ = zero calibration

buildNotes: Power G+ from 5 V (4.5–5.25 V) and G0 from GND. Peak current is up to 300 mA during the lamp pulse, so use a solid 5 V supply and a 100 µF capacitor near the sensor.
The UART pins are 3.3 V logic: cross them (UART_TxD → board RX, UART_RxD → board TX). Settings 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
Read CO2: send FE 04 00 00 00 04 E5 C6; the reply is FE 04 08, then MeterStatus, AlarmStatus, OutputStatus and CO2 (16-bit, big-endian, ppm), then CRC-16/MODBUS low byte first.
Readings settle after about 60 s of warm-up and update every 4 s; there is no point polling faster.
Do not connect Alarm_OC directly to a 3.3 V GPIO: it is pulled up to G+ (5 V) inside the sensor.
ABC (automatic baseline correction) assumes the sensor sees fresh outdoor-level air (about 400 ppm) at least once every 8 days.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from senseair_s8 import S8

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, bits=8, parity=None, stop=1, tx=Pin({UART_RXD}), rx=Pin({UART_TXD}))
sensor = S8(uart)
while True:
    co2, status = sensor.read()
    if status:
        print('S8 status 0x%04x' % status)
    print('CO2=%d ppm' % co2)
    time.sleep(2)
